sections.heading: Where the money comes from — the two-sector map

blocks.text: Development finance draws on distinct pools for each sector. **Public sector**: tax & non-tax revenue (RMI-007), market borrowings (G-secs/SDLs), small savings (NSSF), external assistance (multilateral-bilateral), disinvestment receipts, and monetisation of assets — with the RBI's surplus transfer as the swing item (**~₹2.1-2.7 lakh crore records, 2024-25**). **Private sector**: internal accruals (retained earnings — the largest source for established firms), **bank credit (~₹170+ lakh crore outstanding)**, capital markets (equity IPO/QIP; corporate bonds ~₹47 lakh crore outstanding — bank-dominance's counterweight), NBFC credit, external routes (**FDI, FPI, ECB ~$190 bn era, ADR/GDR**), venture capital-private equity (the startup rail; ~$100+ bn cumulative), and the new rails — **InvITs-REITs, AIFs, crowd-platforms**.

rows: Household savings → finance
Deposits, insurance-pension (EPFO-NPS ~₹25+ lakh crore era), mutual funds (**SIP culture: ~₹25,000+ cr/month; AUM ~₹65+ lakh crore**), direct equity (11+ crore demat)
The financialisation shift — households moving from gold-land to markets: the decade's structural story

The pecking order every answer should state

sections.heading: Evaluation — gaps and the AP lens

items: **The three financing gaps**: (a) **long-tenor infrastructure debt** (banks' ALM limits → NaBFID-InvIT answer); (b) **MSME credit (~₹25-30 lakh crore unmet estimate)** — collateral-and-information problem (account-aggregator, OCEN, TReDS as fintech answers); (c) **risk capital outside metros** — VC's geographic concentration.

**Public-private crowding question**: high government borrowing (~₹14-15 lakh crore gross) can crowd out private credit — but demand-deficient phases show crowding-IN via capex multipliers: state the condition-dependence, don't pick a dogma.

**AP lens**: the state draws on SDLs-NSSF-central loans-EAPs (RMA-014's file); its private sector on bank credit (aqua-agri working capital), the **AP-origin SHG-bank linkage** for micro-enterprise, and port-energy projects on project finance + InvIT-style structures — the two-sector map localised.

sections.heading: Budgetary resources — the tax and non-tax anatomy

rows: **Direct taxes**
Income tax (personal ~₹12+ lakh crore) + corporate (~₹10+ lakh crore); STT-capital gains within
**~55-57% of gross taxes** — the progressivity share at two-decade highs; buoyancy >1 post-tech compliance
**Indirect taxes**
**GST (~₹22+ lakh crore/yr gross; centre's CGST+IGST share)**, customs (~₹2+ lakh crore), central excise (petroleum's residual ~₹3 lakh crore)
GST matured (e-invoicing's evasion squeeze); petroleum excise the un-GST'd cash cow
**Cesses & surcharges**
Health-education cess (4%), infrastructure/agri cesses, income surcharges
**~15-20% of gross taxes, OUTSIDE the divisible pool** — the federal grievance (GBI-020)
**Non-tax revenue**
**RBI + PSB-PSU dividends (~₹3+ lakh crore combined era)**, spectrum-auction receipts, royalties (offshore), interest, fees; **~₹5.5+ lakh crore budgeted highs**
The RBI-transfer dependence question — windfall vs structural
**Non-debt capital receipts**
Disinvestment (~₹50,000 cr targets, chronic shortfalls; strategic sales — Air India 2021 the landmark), asset monetisation (NMP ₹6 lakh cr), loan recoveries
Ambition-execution gap the standing critique

items: **The adequacy question**: tax-GDP ~**11-12% (centre) / ~18% combined** — below OECD (~34%) and emerging peers; the gap = development's financing constraint; drivers — informality, agriculture's exemption, exemption-expenditure (revenue foregone statements), evasion residual.

**The equity audit**: direct-share rising (good); but cess-reliance (unshared + often regressive), petroleum taxation's regressivity, and corporate-cut's distributional optics — equity is direction-positive, composition-mixed.

**The effort agenda**: widen (return-filer base ~8+ crore and growing; TDS-TCS web; AIS data-matching), deepen (GST slab rationalisation done 2025 — revenue-neutrality watch; petroleum-electricity inclusion pending), simplify (Income-tax Act 2025), and stabilise (litigation reduction — ~₹12+ lakh crore locked in disputes: the collection frontier).
**State mirror (AP)**: SOTR anatomy from RMA-012 — SGST > excise > stamps > fuel VAT > vehicles; non-tax thin (mining royalties, interest) — the state's adequacy question is GSDP growth itself.

blocks.text: Exam tip: 'India's tax problem is a base problem, not a rate problem' — then prove it with tax-GDP comparisons, the exemption ledger and the compliance-technology arc.

prelimsPointers: Tax-GDP: centre ~**11-12%**, combined ~**17-18%** — vs OECD ~34%.
Direct taxes ≈ **56-57% of gross taxes** (recent years) — the highest share in decades.
**Cesses & surcharges ~15-20% of gross taxes** — excluded from the divisible pool by Art 270.
Non-tax receipts budgeted at highs (**₹5.5+ lakh crore**) on RBI-PSU dividend strength.
**Revenue foregone** (tax-expenditure) statements accompany the budget — exemptions' fiscal cost.
Disputed direct-tax arrears ≈ **₹12+ lakh crore** — litigation as the locked treasury.
**Air India's strategic sale (2021)** — the disinvestment landmark; NMP targets ₹6 lakh crore monetisation.
Petroleum & alcohol remain outside GST; petroleum excise+VAT is the centre-state cash cow.

Tax growth per unit GDP growth — above one marks a strengthening system.

Shareable net central taxes under Art 270 — cesses' exclusion the federal flashpoint.

sections.heading: Public debt — anatomy of the ₹200-lakh-crore ledger

rows: **Internal market debt**
**Dated G-secs** (5-50 yr; auction-issued; the yield curve's spine) + **T-bills** (91/182/364-day cash management)
The dominant chunk; gross borrowing ~₹14-15 lakh crore/yr
**Small savings (NSSF)**
PPF-NSC-Sukanya-SCSS deposits lent onward to the centre (and once to states/FCI)
The administered-rate parallel pool (~₹ multi-lakh-crore flow)
**External debt (sovereign)**
**Multilateral (WB-ADB-AIIB) + bilateral — only ~2% of central debt, long-tenor, concessional**; no foreign-currency sovereign bonds (the 2019 proposal shelved)
India's conservative signature — insulation from currency-crisis dynamics
**Liabilities beside debt**
Provident-insurance funds (public account), guarantees (contingent), off-budget's cleaned residue
The 'general government' view: **centre ~57%, states ~28-30% → combined ~82-84% of GDP** (peak COVID ~89%)
**States' layer**
SDLs + NSSF legacy + central loans (capex window) + guarantees
AP's file (RMA-014): ~33-35% of GSDP + guarantees

blocks.text: **Loans & grants within receipts**: external assistance arrives as **loans (back-to-back EAPs)** and **grants** (thin, ~welfare-project specific); domestically, the centre's **50-year interest-free capex loans to states (~₹1.5 lakh crore/yr window)** blur the loan-grant line — effectively grant-equivalent transfers with capex conditionality: a fresh instrument worth naming.

items: **Why India's high debt is (so far) safe**: rupee-denominated (~98%), domestically held (banks-insurance-RBI-funds), long average maturity (~12 yrs), captive demand (SLR ~18%) — the **original-sin avoidance** that separates India from EM crisis cases; the cost — financial repression's shadow (captive banks funding the state).

**The r-vs-g test** (GBA-022's frame at national scale): nominal growth (10-11%) above effective interest (~7%) stabilises ratios despite primary deficits — but the margin is cyclical; **interest/revenue ~35-37% (centre)** is the vulnerability metric: India's debt is sustainable AND expensive.

**The reform arc**: FRBM's debt anchor (40/60 targets → the post-FY26 declining-path regime), **JPMorgan-Bloomberg index inclusion (2024-25 — ~$30-40 bn passive inflows, diversifying the holder base)**, retail G-sec access (RBI Retail Direct), and the states' discipline architecture (net-borrowing ceilings, off-budget netting).

**Grants economics**: FC grants (statutory), scheme grants (tied), external grants (minor) — the grant-vs-loan choice embodies the fiscal-federal power question: grants empower, loans discipline; the 50-year interest-free window is the hybrid India invented.

blocks.text: Exam tip: 'India borrowed in its own currency from its own savers for its own tenor — that's why 84% of GDP hasn't meant crisis' — then flag the expense side so the answer isn't complacent.

prelimsPointers: General-government debt ≈ **82-84% of GDP** (peak ~89% FY21); centre ~57%, states ~28-30%.
**External sovereign debt ~2%** of central debt — multilateral-bilateral, concessional; no FX sovereign bonds.
Average maturity of central debt ~**12 years** — among the longest in EMs.
**JPMorgan GBI-EM inclusion (from June 2024)** + Bloomberg (2025): Indian G-secs entered global bond indices (FAR securities).
**SLR (18%)** creates banks' statutory G-sec demand; RBI Retail Direct (2021) opened direct retail access.
**Interest payments ≈ 35-37% of central revenue receipts** — the cost-of-debt vulnerability metric.
**50-year interest-free capex loans** to states (~₹1.3-1.5 lakh crore/yr) — the loan-grant hybrid.
FRBM debt targets: **40% centre / 60% general government**; post-FY26 the anchor is a declining debt path.

glossary.definition: The government's long-tenor bonds forming the sovereign yield curve — public debt's core instrument.
